{{Short description|Armenian management consultant and social entrepreneur (born 1972)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=March 2024}}
'''Avetik Chalabyan''' (Armenian: Ավետիք Չալաբյան, born 21 November 1972) is an Armenian public figure and politician, coordinator of HayaQve National Civic Initiative<ref>https://hayaqve.am/en/%d5%b0%d5%a1%d5%b5%d5%a1%d6%84%d5%be%d5%a5%d5%ab-%d5%a4%d5%a5%d5%b4%d6%84%d5%a5%d6%80/</ref>. Since 2012, he has been participating in and leading political opposition initiatives in Armenia.<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 December 2023 |title=Chalabyan: HayaQve initiative does not pursue any goal of running in Armenia parliamentary election |url=https://news.am/eng/news/799457.html |access-date=2023-12-27 |website=news.am |language=en}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Avetik Chalabyan is a former senior partner of [[McKinsey & Company]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Avetik |language=en |url=https://fast.foundation/en/staff/7172 |access-date=2023-12-29}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=The growing importance of steel scrap in China {{!}} McKinsey |url=https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/metals-and-mining/our-insights/the-growing-importance-of-steel-scrap-in-china |access-date=2023-12-29 |website=www.mckinsey.com}}</ref> Graduated from [[Yerevan State University]] with a master's degree in Theoretical Physics and received his MBA from the [[University of North Carolina]]. Chalabyan led McKinsey's  Metallurgical Practice in CIS and Eastern Europe region from 2010 to 2015, and global Metallurgical Practice from 2015 to 2020. He was  a [[supervisory board]] member of Metinvest, metals and mining group based in [[Netherlands]]. Also served as Head of the WTO Affairs Department at the Ministry of Economic Development of Armenia.

Chalabyan is a co-founder and a member of the board of trustees of Arar Foundation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Avetik Chalabyan |url=https://ararfoundation.am/en/team/avetik-chalabyan/ |access-date=2022-05-17 |website=ARAR FOUNDATION |language=en-US}}</ref> He also serves as a board member in [[Repat Armenia|Repat Armenia Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Board of Trustees |url=https://repatarmenia.org/en/about-us/board-of-trustees |access-date=2022-05-17 |website=repatarmenia.org}}</ref>

== Public and Political activism ==
Chalabyan co-founded the [[National Agenda Party (Armenia)|National Agenda Party]] in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arminfo: National Agenda party established in Armenia |url=https://arminfo.info/full_news.php?id=37963&lang=3 |access-date=2023-12-27 |website=arminfo.info |language=en}}</ref> He left the party in 2020  after the [[Nagorno-Karabakh conflict|44-day war]]. Afterwards he was involved in a number of opposition movements in Armenia, such as the "Unification" initiative implemented in support of Artsakh. Chalabyan was outspoken<ref>{{Cite web |title=Avetik Chalabyan |url=https://mediamax.am/ |access-date=2022-05-17 |website=Mediamax.am |language=en}}</ref> and critical<ref>{{Cite web |date=16 February 2021 |title=Avetik Chalabyan – From Inconceivable Loss to New National Objectives |url=http://repatarmenia.org/en/engage/Inspiration/a/avetik-chalabyan---from-inconceivable-loss-to-new-national-objectives |access-date=2022-05-17 |website=RepatArmenia |language=en}}</ref> about supporting<ref>{{Cite web |last=LLC |first=Helix Consulting |title=Avetik Chalabyan: I call for protecting the rights of the killed Artsakh resident Martin Yeremyan and his brave brother |url=https://www.panorama.am/en/news/2021/11/13/Avetik-Chalabyan/2597899 |access-date=2022-05-17 |website=www.panorama.am |language=en}}</ref> and recognizing [[Republic of Artsakh|Artsakh]],<ref>{{Cite news |title="Armenia should have recognized the Republic of Artsakh on September 27": Avetik Chalabyan |work=Aravot Daily News |url=https://www.aravot-en.am/2022/04/05/301261/}}</ref> consolidation of Armenian diaspora,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Avetik Chalabyan |url=https://regionalpost.org/articles/avetik-chalabyan.html |access-date=2022-05-17 |website=Regional Post |language=en}}</ref> as well as building a stronger defense system<ref>{{Cite web |title=Avetik Chalabyan: "Three keys are needed to open the door" |url=https://mediamax.am/en/news/interviews/17014/ |access-date=2022-05-17 |website=mediamax.am |language=en}}</ref> to assure the sovereignty of the state.

Chalabyan criticized the erosion of democratic institutions in Armenia, advocating for an independent judiciary, the [[rule of law]], and the protection of political and economic freedoms. In addition, he has actively supported educational reform, initiating programs to modernize curricula and provide internationally recognized educational opportunities for Armenian students.<ref>{{cite web |title=Լուրեր Հայաստանից - Tert.am |url=https://tert.am/en/news/2025/01/08/avetik-chalabyan/4219146 |website=tert.am}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Arminfo: We must work hard and persistently so that Armenia never becomes one-party dictatorship - Avetik Chalabyan |url=https://arminfo.info/full_news.php?id=86608&lang=3 |website=arminfo.info |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Россия |first1=McKinsey |title=Путь консультанта: 10 историй о работе в McKinsey, гибкости и филантропических проектах от Аветика Чалабяна |url=https://telegra.ph/Put-konsultanta-10-istorij-o-rabote-v-McKinsey-gibkosti-i-filantropicheskih-proektah-ot-Avetika-CHalabyana-04-11 |website=Telegraph |date=11 April 2018}}</ref>

== HayaQve Initiative ==
In May 2023, Chalabyan co-initiated the civil-legislative initiative Hayakve (Armenian Vote) being the coordinator of its operating headquarters.<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 December 2023 |title=HayaKve initiative submits its draft law to Armenia parliament |url=https://news.am/eng/news/786181.html |access-date=2023-12-27 |website=news.am |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=ՀԱՅԱՔՎԵ – քաղաքացիական օրենսդրական նախաձեռնություն |url=https://hayaqve.am/ |website=hayaqve}}</ref> Launched on June 29, 2023, Hayaqve aimed to mobilize public support to criminalize any recognition of [[Nagorno-Karabakh|Artsakh (Nagorno-Karabakh)]] as part of Azerbaijan and denial or belittling of the [[Armenian genocide]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Hayaqve legislative initiative collects 54,800 signatures |url=https://horizonweekly.ca/en/hayaqve-legislative-initiative-collects-54800-signatures/ |website=[[Horizon Weekly]] |date=29 July 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The Collapse of Artsakh is the Greatest Tragedy That Happened in Our Lifetime. Avetik Chalabyan - Western Armenia TV |url=https://westernarmeniatv.com/en/politics_en/the-collapse-of-artsakh-is-the-greatest-tragedy-that-happened-in-our-lifetime-avetik-chalabyan/ |website=Western Armenia TV |date=19 September 2024}}</ref> The initiative, supported by 66 civic activists, collected over 58,000 signatures, exceeding the required 50,000 to submit the legislative proposal to [[Armenian National Assembly|Armenia's National Assembly]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Hayaqve legislative initiative enters decisive phase |url=https://news.am/eng/news/774222.html |website=[[News.am]] |language=en |date=27 January 2025}}</ref> The proposed amendments to the Criminal Code would impose 10 to 15 years of imprisonment for actions recognizing Artsakh as part of another state or denying the Armenian Genocide.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hayaqve: A referendum called to stop the loss of Artsakh |url=https://regionalpost.org/en/articles/hayaqve-a-referendum-called-to-stop-the-loss-of-artsakh.html |website=Regional Post}}</ref> Despite allegations of administrative obstruction, including refusal of municipal premises for signature collection, the initiative highlighted public resistance to government policies regarding Artsakh.<ref>{{cite web |title=Coordinator of Hayaqve initiative accusing Yerevan Municipality of attempts to torpedo referendum on Artsakh |url=https://arminfo.info/full_news.php?id=77072&lang=3 |website=arminfo.info |language=en}}</ref> Chalabyan criticized the Armenian government's stance on border demarcation and handling of the Artsakh crisis, advocating for national unity, international support, and the preservation of Artsakh’s Armenian identity.<ref>{{cite web |title=“Hayaqve” Submitted a Criminal Application Regarding Border Demarcation - Western Armenia TV |url=https://westernarmeniatv.com/en/politics_en/hayaqve-submitted-a-criminal-application-regarding-border-demarcation/ |website=Western Armenia TV |date=15 May 2024}}</ref> His activism extended to opposing the extradition of Armenian soldiers and commanders to Azerbaijan and urging global powers to address Azerbaijan's actions against Artsakh.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chalabyan: No Armenian soldier and commander should be extradited to Azerbaijan |url=https://news.am/eng/news/782696.html |website=news.am |language=en |date=27 January 2025}}</ref> 

== Political persecution against Avetik Chalabyan ==
In May 2022<ref>https://hy.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022</ref>, during the Resistance Movement, he was detained on charges of allegedly offering material incentives to the chairman of the Student Council of the National Agrarian University of Armenia to attend rallies<ref>https://hy.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D4%B1%D5%BE%D5%A5%D5%BF%D5%AB%D6%84_%D5%89%D5%A1%D5%AC%D5%A1%D5%A2%D5%B5%D5%A1%D5%B6#cite_note-22</ref>. He was released on bail in July 2022<ref>https://hy.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022</ref>. In September 2024<ref>https://hy.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024</ref>, the Court of Appeal vacated the conviction and ordered a retrial<ref>https://hy.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D4%B1%D5%BE%D5%A5%D5%BF%D5%AB%D6%84_%D5%89%D5%A1%D5%AC%D5%A1%D5%A2%D5%B5%D5%A1%D5%B6#cite_note-24</ref>. 

This criminal case was widely criticized by both domestic and international human rights initiatives. The U.S. Department of State<ref>https://hy.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D4%B1%D5%84%D5%86_%D5%8A%D5%A5%D5%BF%D5%A1%D5%AF%D5%A1%D5%B6_%D5%A4%D5%A5%D5%BA%D5%A1%D6%80%D5%BF%D5%A1%D5%B4%D5%A5%D5%B6%D5%BF</ref>, in its 2022 Annual Report on Human Rights in Armenia, categorized Avetik Chalabyan's detention as an instance of arbitrary deprivation of liberty<ref>https://hy.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D4%B1%D5%BE%D5%A5%D5%BF%D5%AB%D6%84_%D5%89%D5%A1%D5%AC%D5%A1%D5%A2%D5%B5%D5%A1%D5%B6#cite_note-25</ref>. In its 2024 report<ref>https://hy.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024</ref>, the Monitoring Committee of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe<ref>https://hy.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D4%B5%D5%BE%D6%80%D5%B8%D5%BA%D5%A1%D5%B5%D5%AB_%D5%AD%D5%B8%D6%80%D5%B0%D6%80%D5%A4%D5%AB_%D4%BD%D5%B8%D6%80%D5%B0%D6%80%D5%A4%D5%A1%D6%80%D5%A1%D5%B6%D5%A1%D5%AF%D5%A1%D5%B6_%D5%BE%D5%A5%D5%B0%D5%A1%D5%AA%D5%B8%D5%B2%D5%B8%D5%BE</ref>, in reference to Chalabyan’s arrest, noted that encouraging participation in assemblies should not be subject to criminal regulation unless such encouragement conflicts with laws establishing proportionate restrictions on campaign financing<ref>https://hy.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D4%B1%D5%BE%D5%A5%D5%BF%D5%AB%D6%84_%D5%89%D5%A1%D5%AC%D5%A1%D5%A2%D5%B5%D5%A1%D5%B6#cite_note-26</ref>.

On June 23, 2026, new public criminal proceedings were initiated against Avetik Chalabyan under Article 43-210, Part 2, Clauses 5 and 6 of the RA Criminal Code, charging him with preparation to obstruct the exercise of voting rights of a group of people. Chalabyan rejected the charges, characterizing them as entirely false.

In the lead-up to Avetik Chalabyan's detention, an unverified and edited audio recording surfaced on June 6, 2026—the day of electoral silence preceding the Parliamentary elections—on Baghramyan 26, a Telegram channel associated with pro-government narrative dissemination, where Chalabyan is allegedly holding discussions with Russian-speaking individuals concerning the upcoming Parliamentary elections in Armenia. Both the origin and the authenticity of the recording remain undetermined.

According to human rights advocates, the selection of pretrial detention as a preventive measure against Avetik Chalabyan serves not to ensure the smooth course of the investigation, but rather as a punishment—a practice explicitly prohibited under domestic legislation and international conventions. Furthermore, a ban on visits from Chalabyan’s family members—including his underage child—and Members of the National Assembly has been imposed. Human rights advocates have characterized these restrictions as a deliberate attempt to completely isolate and psychologically pressure the political figure.

== Criticism of the Criminal Case ==
The [[US Embassy]] in Armenia included Chalabyan's case in 2022 [[Human Rights Report]] as an example of [[Arbitrary arrest and detention|arbitrary arrest]] by the local authorities.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Armenia |first=U. S. Mission |date=28 April 2023 |title=2022 Human Rights Report on Armenia |url=https://am.usembassy.gov/2022-human-rights-report/ |access-date=2023-12-27 |website=U.S. Embassy in Armenia |language=en-US}}</ref>

[[Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe]] addressed the case of Chalabyan stressing the problematic nature of the Armenian criminal law noting that incentivizing participation in rallies should not be criminalized and the use made of the criminal code in this case is disturbing.<ref>{{Cite web |date=17 May 2024 |title=The honouring of obligations and commitments by Armenia |url=https://rm.coe.int/the-honouring-of-obligations-and-commitments-by-armenia/1680afc0a1}}</ref>

[[Freedom House]] reported it is unusual move that court banned activist Avetik Chalabyan from participating in public rallies for two years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Armenia: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report |url=https://freedomhouse.org/country/armenia/freedom-world/2024 |access-date=2024-12-11 |website=Freedom House |language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Avetik Chalabyan is married and has four children.<ref>{{Citation |title=Moments of Sincerity with Avetik Chalabyan |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yZms5DA67MI |language=en |access-date=2022-05-17}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Ավետիք Չալաբյան |url=https://mediamax.am/am/authors/1266/ |website=Mediamax.am |language=en}}</ref>
